records.label: spacr.mask_io#9
records.source: Every object is one feature, ROI or annotation, carrying its object type (``cell``, ``nucleus`` ...), its object id and its class; the class defaults to the object type. Each object is traced on its own, so objects that touch stay separate. Outlines follow PIXEL EDGES, not pixel centres: a pixel ``(row, col)`` is the square from ``x = col`` to ``col + 1`` and ``y = row`` to ``row + 1``, the convention QuPath and ImageJ both use. A pixel is inside a polygon when its centre is, so a traced outline rasterised back gives the object exactly: no tolerance, holes and several-part objects included. A hole is an interior ring (GeoJSON), a path of a composite ROI (ImageJ) or, since a COCO polygon cannot have one, an RLE segmentation (COCO).

A pixel is inside a polygon when its centre is, so a traced outline rasterised back gives the object exactly: no tolerance, holes and several-part objects included. A hole is an interior ring (GeoJSON), a path of a composite ROI (ImageJ) or, since a COCO polygon cannot have one, an RLE segmentation (COCO).
records.translation: Cada objeto es una entidad, una ROI o una anotación, con su tipo de objeto (``cell``, ``nucleus`` ...), su id de objeto y su clase; la clase es por defecto el tipo de objeto. Cada objeto se traza por separado, así que los objetos que se tocan siguen separados. Los contornos siguen los bordes de los píxeles, no sus centros: un píxel ``(row, col)`` es el cuadrado de ``x = col`` a ``col + 1`` y de ``y = row`` a ``row + 1``, la convención que usan tanto QuPath como ImageJ. Un píxel está dentro de un polígono cuando lo está su centro, de modo que un contorno trazado y rasterizado de nuevo devuelve exactamente el objeto: sin tolerancia, con agujeros y objetos de varias partes incluidos. Un agujero es un anillo interior (GeoJSON), una trayectoria de una ROI compuesta (ImageJ) o, como un polígono COCO no puede tenerlo, una segmentación RLE (COCO).

records.label: spacr.sp_stats#4
records.source: :func:`score_arrayed_screen` scores every well of an arrayed screen against its negative control: robust z (median/MAD), SSMD with the method-of-moments, UMVUE and robust estimators for designs with and without replicates (Zhang 2011, J Biomol Screen 16:775), and the B-score (Brideau et al. 2003), whose row and column effects come from :func:`median_polish`, a port of R's ``stats::medpolish``. Scores are computed per plate or against the pooled negative control, hits are called at chosen thresholds, and :func:`write_hit_report` writes the ranked hit table as CSV and one plate heatmap per statistic through :func:`spacr.plot.save_figure`. Wells are located by :mod:`spacr.plate_qc` and controls named in the :mod:`spacr.well_spec` notation, and the per-plate Z' comes from the control-chart screen's own :func:`~spacr.qt.widgets.control_chart.zprime_frame`.
records.context: :func:`score_arrayed_screen` scores every microplate sample position of an arrayed screen against its negative control: robust z (median/MAD), SSMD with the method-of-moments, UMVUE and robust estimators for designs with and without replicates (Zhang 2011, J Biomol Screen 16:775), and the B-score (Brideau et al. 2003), whose row and column effects come from :func:`median_polish`, a port of R's ``stats::medpolish``. Scores are computed per laboratory microplate or against the pooled negative control, hits are called at chosen thresholds, and :func:`write_hit_report` writes the ranked hit table as CSV and one laboratory microplate heatmap per statistic through :func:`spacr.plot.save_figure`. Microplate sample positions are located by :mod:`spacr.plate_qc` and controls named in the :mod:`spacr.well_spec` notation, and the per-laboratory microplate Z' comes from the control-chart screen's own :func:`~spacr.qt.widgets.control_chart.zprime_frame`.
records.translation: :func:`score_arrayed_screen` puntúa cada pocillo de un cribado en formato de matriz frente a su control negativo: z robusta (mediana/MAD), SSMD con el método de los momentos, UMVUE y estimadores robustos para diseños con y sin réplicas (Zhang 2011, J Biomol Screen 16:775), y la puntuación B (Brideau et al. 2003), cuyos efectos de fila y columna proceden de :func:`median_polish`, una adaptación de ``stats::medpolish`` de R. Las puntuaciones se calculan por placa o frente al control negativo agrupado, los aciertos se determinan con los umbrales elegidos y :func:`write_hit_report` escribe la tabla de aciertos ordenada como CSV y un mapa de calor de placa por estadístico mediante :func:`spacr.plot.save_figure`. Los pocillos se localizan con :mod:`spacr.plate_qc` y los controles se nombran en la notación de :mod:`spacr.well_spec`, y el Z' por placa procede del propio :func:`~spacr.qt.widgets.control_chart.zprime_frame` de la vista del gráfico de control.

records.source: The profiling helpers turn Measure's per-object tables into well and treatment profiles and score them, following pycytominer and copairs so the numbers agree with those tools on the same features. Each object table is aggregated to a per-well median, a plate map adds the treatment annotations, features are normalised plate by plate against the negative-control wells (robust MAD by default), uninformative and redundant features are removed (variance, frequency, correlation, missing values and outliers), and replicate wells are collapsed into consensus profiles. Replicate reproducibility is scored as mean average precision (mAP) with copairs' permutation null and Benjamini-Hochberg correction: phenotypic activity (replicates against controls) and, given a phenotype label, phenotypic consistency (treatments that share the label). Percent replicating is reported beside it. Profiles are written as CSV and Parquet with ``Metadata_`` columns, the consensus also as GCT, with an mAP plot and a consensus-similarity heatmap. Measure runs the whole recipe at the end of a run when ``profiling`` is on.
records.context: The profiling helpers turn Measure's per-object tables into well and treatment profiles and score them, following pycytominer and copairs so the numbers agree with those tools on the same features. Each object table is aggregated to a per-well median, a laboratory microplate map adds the treatment annotations, features are normalised laboratory microplate by laboratory microplate against the negative-control microplate sample positions (robust MAD by default), uninformative and redundant features are removed (variance, frequency, correlation, missing values and outliers), and replicate microplate sample positions are collapsed into consensus profiles. Replicate reproducibility is scored as mean average precision (mAP) with copairs' permutation null and Benjamini-Hochberg correction: phenotypic activity (replicates against controls) and, given a phenotype label, phenotypic consistency (treatments that share the label). Percent replicating is reported beside it. Profiles are written as CSV and Parquet with ``Metadata_`` columns, the consensus also as GCT, with an mAP plot and a consensus-similarity heatmap. Measure runs the whole recipe at the end of a run when ``profiling`` is on.
records.translation: Las funciones auxiliares de perfilado convierten las tablas por objeto de Measure en perfiles por pocillo y por tratamiento y los puntúan, siguiendo a pycytominer y copairs para que las cifras coincidan con esas herramientas sobre las mismas características. Cada tabla de objetos se agrega a una mediana por pocillo, un mapa de placa añade las anotaciones de tratamiento, las características se normalizan placa a placa frente a los pocillos de control negativo (MAD robusta por defecto), se eliminan las características poco informativas y redundantes (varianza, frecuencia, correlación, valores ausentes y atípicos) y los pocillos réplica se agrupan en perfiles de consenso. La reproducibilidad de las réplicas se puntúa como mean average precision (mAP) con la distribución nula por permutación de copairs y la corrección de Benjamini-Hochberg: actividad fenotípica (réplicas frente a controles) y, dada una etiqueta de fenotipo, consistencia fenotípica (tratamientos que comparten la etiqueta).
